subject: SparkLaunch credits — proposal for invoice anchoring and onboarding sweetener
messages:
From: Aisha Kapoor <aisha@stellarfoundry.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stellarfoundry.ai
Date: 2025-05-12T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: SparkLaunch credits — convert to reserved capacity?

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the support during SparkLaunch — StellarFoundry was excited to participate. We currently have an unused portion of our award (roughly $48,200 in platform credits) and are evaluating a move from sandbox/hosted to Dedicated for predictable throughput.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood convert remaining SparkLaunch credits into an invoice credit that we can apply to a Dedicated reservation?
- If conversion to invoice credit isn’t possible, what packaging/discount flexibility do you offer for a 12-month reserved commit (we'd likely start with 3–4 GPUs equivalent)?

Attached: MVP usage export and the award letter so you can see the credit scope. Procurement is cc'd (procurement@stellarfoundry.ai) — they’ll own PO if we land on terms.

Key constraints on our side: we need predictable billing cadence for our finance team and a signed addendum by end of month if possible. Can you outline feasible options and any required paperwork?

Best,
Aisha Kapoor
CEO, StellarFoundry
[attachment: MVP-usage_report.csv (CSV, 42KB)]
[attachment: sparklaunch-award-letter.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Kapoor <aisha@stellarfoundry.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-12T12:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SparkLaunch credits — convert to reserved capacity?

Hi Aisha — great to hear from you and congrats again on the SparkLaunch work. Appreciate the attachments; I reviewed the usage file. Quick outline of practical options (so procurement can pick):

Option A — Simple invoice credit (fastest):
- Convert credits at 60% face value as a one-time invoice credit applied to the first invoice for Dedicated.
- Estimated credit value applied: $48,200 * 0.60 = $28,920.
- No change to standard T&Cs; addendum signs to acknowledge credit application.

Option B — Onboarding sweetener + committed discount (recommended for runway):
- Onboarding credit: apply 40% of credit value as an onboarding credit (applied before month 1 billing).
- Committed discount: 15% off list for the first 12 months on a 12-month reserved commit of at least the equivalent of 3–4 GPUs.
- If they commit to >=12 months we also offer a 30-day migration support credit (engineering hours) to help move KV/caching and inference tuning.

Operational notes:
- We prefer to structure the invoice credit as a credit memo applied to the first invoice (Option A) or as a line-item credit + signed addendum (Option B).
- We’ll need a PO or signature to bind the committed discount.

Next steps: if either option looks good I’ll loop in Finance & Legal to produce a short addendum (I’ve attached a draft addendum v1 for reference). Can we jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to lock scope?

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: proposed_addendum_v1.pdf (PDF, 28KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: 2025-05-12T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SparkLaunch credits — approvals for credit conversion and invoice anchoring

Team — forwarding the ask from StellarFoundry (cc'd procurement). They want either an invoice credit or packaging/discount on a 12-month Dedicated commit. Summary and approvals needed:

Proposal (what I would like to offer):
- Convert credits at 60% face value as an invoice credit applied to first invoice (fastest path).
- OR: Offer hybrid Option B: 40% onboarding credit applied up-front + 15% first-year committed discount for 12-month reservation. Engineering migration credit (30 days) as a customer success sweetener.

What I need from you:
- Lauren (Finance): confirm we can book a credit memo of $28,920 vs. treating as revenue reduction; any tax/AR implications we should flag? If Option B, confirm how to route the onboarding credit and how to record the committed discount in billing.
- Karthik (RevOps): any quota/commission adjustments for this conversion? Need to avoid surprises on AE comp if we treat credits as a one-time offset.
- Ben (Partnerships): confirm the migration support credit cadence and whether CS/PS can commit to the 30-day engagement window.
- Legal: if helpful I can send the addendum redline; main ask is an acknowledgement of credit conversion and a simple clause for committed discount term.

Attachments: Jordan's proposed_addendum_v1.pdf (simple addendum template), internal MA plan link with numbers.

If I don’t hear objections by EOD tomorrow I’ll share Option B as the recommended path to StellarFoundry and ask for PO/PO number.

Thanks,
Jordan

[Internal links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-ma-action-plan]

From: Aisha Kapoor <aisha@stellarfoundry.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stellarfoundry.ai
Date: 2025-05-14T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SparkLaunch credits — convert to reserved capacity?

Jordan — thanks for the clear options and the addendum draft. Procurement and finance reviewed and we prefer Option B with one small tweak:

- Accept onboarding credit at 40% of award (apply as a prepayment / credit against month 1 invoices).
- Committed discount: 15% for 12 months on a 12-month reserved commit (we’ll confirm exact GPU sizing in the PO).
- Request that the onboarding credit appear on the invoice as a dedicated line (for our audit), and that the addendum references our PO number.

We can sign the short addendum and issue PO STELLAR-PO-5588 if Redwood legal is comfortable with the redline Jordan shared. Procurement will attach the PO once we have final language.

Procurement contact: procurement@stellarfoundry.ai

Happy to hop on a call if you want to walk through invoicing flow.

Best,
Aisha
CEO, StellarFoundry
